summary:
PyroVerse is a geospatial monitoring web platform that harmonizes and analyzes fire hotspot data collected by MODIS and VIIRS sensors. The project overcomes the challenge of integrating satellite observations with varying spatial resolutions, detection characteristcis, and data formats. This provides a more consistent and comprehensive view of fire activity.
The plataform facilitates data visualization, organizing information in a way that makes it easy to explore geographic distribution, compare historical data, monitor monthly and annual trends, and identify anomalous variations formats, such as tables, charts, cards etc. By combining information from multiple satellite sources, PyroVerse improves data interpretation and supports more reliable environmental monitoring.
Accurate and accessible wildfire information is important because it can contribute to faster analysis, better-informed decisions, and more effective strategies for preventing and managing forest fires.
details:
How it works

PyroVerse is a geospatial data visualization and analysis platform that compiles wildfire hotspot data collected by MODIS and VIIRS satellites. PyroVerse organizes detection records and provides interactive visualizations, allowing users to explore fire occurrences from geographic and temporal perspectives.
The platform includes historical comparisons spanning several years (2000-2025), charts displaying the monthly distribution of fire hotspots, trend analyses, and anomaly identification. Users can explore details about detections, including the satellite source, sensor type, confidence level, fire radiative power, and geographic coordinates.

Benefits and Intended Impact

By making satellite data easier to explore and interpret, PyroVerse helps users identify patterns, observe changes in wildfire activity, and recognize unusual variations in hotspot records. Its intended impact is to support environmental monitoring, improve access to relevant information, and contribute to more informed decision-making regarding wildfire prevention and management.

Technologies and Tools

The project was developed using Python, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, SQL (DuckDB and SQLite), Streamlit, Plotly, NumPy, pandas, PyArrow, Globe.gl, Figma, Visual Studio Code, Git and Github. Satellite hotspot information from MODIS and VIIRS serves as the primary data source.

Creativity and Innovation

The project's main innovation lies in bringing information from two different satellite monitoring systems into a unified analytical environment. Instead of simply displaying individual detections, PyroVerse emphasizes historical analysis, comparative visualization, and the identification of unusual patterns.

Factors Considered

During development, the team considered data consistency, temporal and geographic accuracy, visualization clarity, and user experience. These factors guided the organization of information and the design of the platform, aiming to make complex satellite observations more understandable and useful.
